description: Neighbours who fix things together every Saturday - bikes, toasters, fences, friendships. Knowledge is shared, never sold.
name: Repair Café Collective

value_cards.because: Expertise has been used as gatekeeping for too long. The person who teaches ten people to fix bikes has done more than the person who fixed a hundred.
value_cards.care_about: Treating technical skill as something to give away, not hoard — the highest act of skill is creating the conditions where you are no longer needed.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Expert capture — repairs that only one person can do, creating permanent dependency.
value_cards.in_conflict: The learner over the efficiency of the fix.
looks_like: Welcoming complete beginners and giving them the first tool to try
Never making someone feel stupid for not knowing something technical
Writing guides in plain language and leaving them where others will find them
value_cards.never_do: Take over a repair from someone who is learning, just because it's faster.
value_cards.title: Knowledge belongs to whoever needs it

value_cards.because: Every object that gets repaired rather than replaced is a material extracted from the earth, a worker paid to make it, and a landfill site it never fills.
value_cards.care_about: Making the first response to any broken thing a serious attempt to fix it — and building the skills and tools to make that possible.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Repair Café as a feel-good event where the same five people fix things for admiring spectators.
value_cards.in_conflict: The person who leaves knowing how over the person who leaves with a working thing.
looks_like: Bringing the broken thing to the café before looking for a replacement
Documenting the repair so the next person can do it themselves
Teaching repair skills explicitly, not just doing the repair for someone
value_cards.never_do: Fix something without explaining what was broken and why.
value_cards.title: Repair over replace
